Hi John / Sabrina 	6

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to validate your performance SLAs for a Private/VPC deployment:

Summary from call:
- Target latency: p95 <= 120ms end-to-end for streaming API under production traffic (we discussed aiming for p95 <= 100ms where possible)
- Throughput/concurrency: baseline 100 concurrent streams, spike to 500 concurrent for peak batch jobs
- Streaming requirements: chunked server->client streaming with per-token latency constraint (aim <50ms token emission after model response ready)
- Network topology: traffic will flow from ACME application servers in us-west-2 -> transit VPC (VPC peering or Transit Gateway) -> Redwood Private nodes in your VPC; encryption in transit via TLS; VPN currently considered as fallback
- Egress: ACME indicated strict egress auditing; need to confirm allowed egress IP ranges, and whether proxy must be used

Immediate asks (what we need to validate next):
1) Can you share a simple network diagram and the IP ranges for any NAT / egress gateways (attachment: rdw-network-checklist-v1.pdf)
2) Can NetOps run a traceroute / mtr to the proposed Redwood endpoint and paste results (or attach) so we can estimate internal latency and hops?
3) Confirm whether you will use VPC Peering, Transit Gateway, or an IPsec VPN for connectivity. If VPN, provide expected crypto profiles and throughput caps.
4) Do you have an internal SLO budget for network (e.g., allocate <=30ms one-way for internal network to meet end-to-end p95 <120ms)?
5) Are there any deep packet inspection/proxies that might buffer or reassemble streaming connections?

Next steps / timeline:
- If you can share the traceroute + diagram by Monday (3/15), our SRE (Jordan) will run a quick perf model and return a short risk assessment + recommended config for peering or VPN.
- If network looks green, we schedule a 30-45 minute on-net test (simulated load) the week of 3/22.

I pasted a short network checklist in the attached PDF for NetOps. Happy to jump on another call with NetOps to walk through specifics.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks for the traceroute, John 	6 this is helpful. A few quick notes from SRE:

- 45-55ms RTT from app to endpoint is reasonable. One-way network budget ~25-30ms supports your target p95 <=120ms if model execution stays ~60-70ms p95. We should validate model latency under realistic token lengths.
- For streaming workloads, we recommend keeping TCP keepalive and disabling any proxy-level buffering (some egress proxies will buffer chunked responses).
- Suggested peering config: Transit Gateway with static routes to Redwood nodes + BGP community to prefer low-latency path. If TGW is not supported, VPC peering between app VPC and Redwood VPC (cross-account) is next best.
- If you expect SSL/TLS termination at your proxy, confirm that it supports HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1 chunked responses; HTTP/2 gives better multiplexing for concurrency.

Action items we can take on our side:
- I can spin up a short perf test harness that replays streaming traffic at 100 concurrent streams and measures server-side model token emission latency. We just need an ephemeral test CIDR and one app instance IP to allowlist.
- Rishi will prepare a short doc outlining peering vs VPN tradeoffs for your network team.

Marissa 	6 if you want, schedule the NetOps sync for Wed 3/17 10am PT and we'll bring the perf harness.

Jordan
